2. The suit out of which the appeal arose was instituted by the respondents for a declaration of titles to and recovery of possession of the lands in dispute by evicting the appellants therefrom. The suit was decreed by Mr. N. Hossain, Subordinate Judge, Dinajpur in title suit No. 22 of 1965. On appeal, Mr. M. M. Hoq, District Judge, Dinajpur upheld the findings of the trial Court but found that the trial Court did not frame any issue on the point of limitation nor considered the matter at all. He, therefore, felt that the suit should be sent back on remand to decide the question as to whether it was barred by limitation. 

 3. To decide the correctness of the procedure adopted by the learned District Judge, it is necessary to consider the provisions relating to remand contained in the Code of Civil Procedure. In section 107 of the Code it has been provided that subject to such conditions and limitations as may be prescribed an appellate Court shall have the power to remand the case. This creates general jurisdiction to remand a case, to the lower Court. The expression "Subject to such conditions and limitations as may be prescribed" would indicate that this power is to be exercised in accordance with the rules provided in Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure.  5. Having regards to the facts involved in the present case Mr. M.H. Khondker, the learned Advocate for the Appellants, expressed his grave doubts as to the validity of the course adopted by the learned District Judge in deciding all the issues excepting the one relating to limitation which he sent back to the trial Court for its decisions. He contended that as this case did neither fall under Order 41, rule 23 inasmuch as the trial Court has not disposed of this suit upon a preliminary point and the decree has not been reversed in appeal nor it came under the purview of rule 23-A which empowered the appellate Court to send back the case for retrial, if the trial Court and disposed of the case otherwise then on a preliminary point, the only provisions which should have guided the learned District Judge are contained in Order 41, rule 25. In support of his contention he cited the decision in the case of Rakhit Mahanta & ors, Vs. Puddo Bauri and ors. Reported in 9 C.W.N. 54 and the case of Amvica Churn Das Vs. Kala Chandra Das reported in 10 C.W.N. 422. 

 10. For the reasons and circumstances discussed above we set aside the judgment and order of the lower appellate Court and direct the judge to follow the procedure laid down in Order 41, rule 25 C.P.C. keeping this appeal pending in his Court and call for a finding of the trial Court on the issue of limitation. After receiving the finding from the trial Court he shall determine the appeal in accordance with the provisions of Order 41, rule 25 C.P.C.
